drills.q: True or false: a Scala Future starts executing only when you call .map or await it.
drills.a: False -- Futures start eagerly on construction using the implicit ExecutionContext. (Laziness is what IO/ZIO provide, or Future { ... } wrapped in a by-name call-by-need structure.)

drills.q: Name two things a case class generates that a Java record does not.
drills.a: copy() for named-field cloning and unapply-based pattern matching wired into match expressions (records gained deconstruction patterns only in Java 21). Also case classes can extend traits/classes; records are implicitly final.

drills.q: A service on the global ExecutionContext slows to a crawl under load with zero errors. Diagnose.
drills.a: Classic blocking-on-global-pool starvation: JDBC/HTTP calls park all ForkJoinPool threads (sized = cores) while tasks queue; logs show latency not failures. Fix: dedicated pools per blocking source or effect-runtime blocking brackets.

drills.q: Why can't Catalyst optimize Python UDFs the way it optimizes Scala Dataset lambdas?
drills.a: Scala lambdas in typed Datasets are JVM closures Catalyst can inspect/inline into the plan; Python UDFs cross a process boundary with serialization per row (narrowed by Arrow columnar batches since Spark 2.3 but never eliminated).

drills.q: Your company's revenue exceeds Akka's BSL threshold. Three legal paths forward?
drills.a: 1) Migrate to Apache Pekko (Apache 2.0 fork, namespace-change tooling exists); 2) purchase Lightbend subscription/license; 3) freeze on last Apache-licensed versions (security risk accrues). Migration is the standard answer.

drills.q: Can a Scala 2.13 application depend on a library published with Scala 3.8?
drills.a: No -- the TASTy reader ceiling is Scala 3.7 for 2.13 consumers; 3.8+ artifacts are unreadable. The reverse direction (Scala 3 consuming 2.13 artifacts) remains supported indefinitely.

drills.q: Greenfield CRUD service, Java-only team, no Spark anywhere. Pick the stack and defend in one sentence each.
drills.a: Java 21: records/sealed interfaces/switch patterns/virtual threads deliver Scala's everyday wins natively with a bigger hiring pool; Kotlin if null-safety and concision matter more than ecosystem orthodoxy; Scala buys compile friction and FP learning curve here for marginal gain.

drills.q: What do virtual threads NOT give you that ZIO/Cats Effect do?
drills.a: Cancellation-as-value, retry policies, timeouts-as-values, fiber supervision/structured joins, and resource brackets (acquire/release guaranteed on failure). Virtual threads fix blocking cost, not correctness tooling for concurrent composition.

drills.q: Either[String, User] vs throwing UserNotFoundException: which for 'user not found' in a domain API and why?
drills.a: Either -- absence of a user is an expected, recoverable outcome that belongs in the signature so callers must handle it (flatMap short-circuit or mapped error response). Exceptions suit bugs/infrastructure failures, not modeled outcomes.
